replies.author: Ghostbrain77
replies.body:
Perspective of someone from the US who has done a little research into modern Chinese work culture but not enough where I’m not willing to accept differing perspectives:

They are pro government, but the government is much more geared towards “the people” than the US as an example, yes. They have streamlined local/district(not the right word) government very efficiently to allow better response by the party to the needs of the people. Yet many industries are just as brutal on workers if not more than western ones. You will have a roof over your head and food, but might be working 60 hours a week. There is no separate union from the one run by the state, your opinions/suggestions have to be run through the filter of “how does this affect the party?”.

Still it all depends upon the global competition/if the industry is local or international focused. Hierarchy is near absolute there, with the state getting final say though. You do not get to say no to the boss. As always, there is a trade off. Security in exchange for autonomy. Fairness (as defined by the state) in exchange for flexibility or independent achievement.

replies.author: Ghostbrain77
replies.body: Extra reply to say that I don’t say any of this in direct judgement of China, but because I find it interesting. Chinas ambition is both respectable and scary to me.

comments.author: EmperorsShadow
comments.body: The effort spent on it matters a lot more than if its Ai or not. They definitely polished it. There is like 8+ hours of footage in it that made the cut, so the actual process likely took months if not years. The story is quite solid. 30 voice actors, and video editors who understand cinematography to sort though hundreds of hours of generated footage not to mention  the storyboarding and the lora+storyboarding+sketching to generate the right footage. On top of that the amount of compute used is likely not cheap. So its a team of funded professionals who spent months on it.

comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body:
FMV games are barely games to begin with and in this case most of it is just down to video gen.

From the trailer it doesn't look great imo. Almost every person has that fake specular AI skin look and AI face. It also looks completely incohesive like it's just a bunch of clips from different movies all thrown together. It's even jumping between realistic and a CG video game cut scene look.

I would as also be highly skeptical of the claim that all the voices are real humans. Why would a person or studio make their entire game using AI, then decide to pay a whole bunch of voice actors. It doesn't make sense. I wouldn't be surprised if they just used cloned real voices to use with AI.

It looks like it's had a decent amount of work put into it which is elevating it above the usual AI slop level but I doubt it would go down as well with a western audience.
